vuln_id: ARVO arvo:52006 / lldpd CDP address parsing over-read

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this prepared checkout. Its `src/daemon/protocols/cdp.c:480` matches the saved ASan crash line, while the metadata vulnerable commit has the same buggy logic with different formatting and line numbers.

classification.classification_note: ASan reports `heap-buffer-overflow`, but the source-level defect is stale remaining-length bookkeeping inside the CDP Addresses TLV parser, which admits a later 2-byte read past the end of the heap-backed frame buffer.

bug_description.original: A read overflow occurs in the daemon when parsing CDP addresses.
bug_description.original_source: sample metadata / patch.diff / saved Stage 01 sanitizer trace / staged vulnerable source / static parse of the staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 120-byte raw frame. In `cdp_decode`, the parser reaches an Addresses TLV whose header bytes are `00 02 00 4d`, so `tlv_type == CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES` and `tlv_len == 73`. `addresses_len` is initialized to 69 after subtracting the 4-byte address-count field, and the next four bytes set `nb = 0x20202020`, so the loop does not terminate before its length checks. In the first address iteration, the parser consumes protocol-type `0x20`, protocol-length `0x01`, protocol byte `0x20`, and then reads address length `0x0020`, so 32 address-body bytes are discarded. The bug is that `PEEK_DISCARD(address_len)` advances `pos` and shrinks the real parser `length`, but vulnerable code forgets to apply the same 32-byte decrement to `addresses_len`. After `PEEK_RESTORE(pos_next_address)`, the parser is positioned at the second address with only 32 actual TLV bytes left while `addresses_len` still says 64. In the second iteration, the next bytes again make `address_len == 32`; the guard `addresses_len < address_len + 2` evaluates false as `62 < 34`, even though only 30 real bytes remain after reading those two header bytes. `PEEK_DISCARD(address_len)` therefore moves `pos` two bytes past the 120-byte heap buffer, and the subsequent `PEEK_UINT16` at `cdp.c:480` performs the saved 2-byte out-of-bounds read. The fix adds the missing `addresses_len -= address_len` immediately after discarding each address body.

source.description: Source step. This is the first project statement on the crashing path that reads the attacker-controlled Addresses-TLV header and materializes the dispatch state for the vulnerable address parser.
source.value_from: Static parsing of the staged `poc` shows that bytes 43-44 are `00 02`, so this statement reads `tlv_type == CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES` from the witness and selects the address-decoding case.
source.note: Scored source step. The harness call into `cdp_decode()` is not scored; this TLV-header read is the first project statement that consumes the witness bytes needed for the vulnerable path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted scalar is the per-TLV remaining-byte counter `addresses_len` that later drifts away from the real parser `length`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged witness, the Addresses TLV length field is `00 4d`, so step 2 computes `tlv_len == 73` and this statement initializes `addresses_len == 69` after removing the 4-byte address-count field.
tainted_value_origin.note: All later subframe guards compare against this counter, so once it is left 32 bytes too large the parser admits the out-of-bounds path.

sink.description: ASan sink. This 16-bit read occurs after the second-iteration discard has already moved `pos` two bytes past the heap-backed frame buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 2` in `cdp_decode` at `src/daemon/protocols/cdp.c:480:19`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After discarding an address body, vulnerable code advances the real parser position but fails to subtract the same `address_len` from `addresses_len`, so later bounds checks overestimate the bytes still available in the TLV.
root_cause.note: The staged fix inserts `addresses_len -= address_len;` immediately after this exact statement.

parser_admitted.description: The witness reaches the vulnerable parser arm because the current TLV header decodes as type `0x0002`, so `cdp_decode()` enters the Addresses case instead of treating the TLV as unknown.

evidence_limitations: The prepared Stage 01 checkout is commit `4755f186d1c889ac3525faffbaa820b8d760f153`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `e1af9ac6424f32d04c9ec08914ebb132206f1110`. The fine trace is therefore anchored to the staged checkout that actually produced the saved ASan report, and the patch diff is used to confirm the missing state update.

The fuzzer harness file `FuzzDecode.c` is an untracked workspace artifact rather than a file present in the metadata vulnerable commit. It is used only as crash-stack context; all scored source, root-cause, and sink anchors are in project file `src/daemon/protocols/cdp.c`.

coarse_trace.summary: The witness TLV header decodes as `CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES` with total length `0x004d`, so `cdp_decode()` enters the address parser and initializes `addresses_len` from attacker-controlled TLV bytes.
The same TLV advertises `nb = 0x20202020` addresses; in the first iteration the parser reads a 32-byte address body and advances past it.
Because vulnerable code does not execute `addresses_len -= address_len` after that first 32-byte body, the real parser `length` drops to 32 while `addresses_len` stays 64.

On the second iteration the stale counter lets the guard `addresses_len < address_len + 2` pass for another 32-byte address body even though only 30 real bytes remain after reading the two header bytes.
The second 32-byte discard moves `pos` two bytes past the 120-byte heap buffer, and the next `PEEK_UINT16` performs the saved out-of-bounds 2-byte read at `cdp.c:480`.

fine_trace.note: Source step. At witness offsets 43-44, this read materializes `tlv_type == 0x0002`, selecting the CDP Addresses parser.
The next two witness bytes are `00 4d`, so this computes `tlv_len == 73`, meaning the Addresses TLV body spans exactly the remaining 73 bytes of the 106-byte CDP payload.
Entering `case CDP_TLV_ADDRESSES`, the parser removes the 4-byte address-count field from `tlv_len` and initializes the subframe remaining-length counter to `69`.
The next four bytes are `20 20 20 20`, so this reads `nb == 0x20202020`. The loop therefore stays live beyond the first address and relies on the internal length checks to stop safely.

In the first loop iteration, after consuming protocol-type `0x20`, protocol-length `0x01`, and one protocol byte, this statement reads the first address-body length from bytes `00 20`, so `address_len == 32` while `addresses_len` becomes `64`.
The first address-length guard uses the still-synchronized values `64 < 32`, so it does not reject the 32-byte body and execution proceeds to the discard.

Root-cause step. This discards the 32-byte first address body and reduces the real parser `length` from `64` to `32`, but vulnerable code does not also execute `addresses_len -= address_len`, so `addresses_len` incorrectly stays `64`.

After the IPv4 probe rewinds and replays the first subframe, this restore returns the parser to the end of the first address with the true remaining `length == 32`, while the stale bookkeeping variable from step 7 is still `addresses_len == 64`.

In the second iteration, after discarding one protocol-type byte, this reads the next byte `0x20` as `address_len == 32`. The stale counter becomes `62`, but the real parser `length` has already fallen to `30` because only 32 bytes were left at the start of the iteration.

This is the critical present-but-defeated guard. With the stale variable it checks `62 < 34` and falls through, even though the real parser has only `30` bytes left and cannot safely skip another 32-byte body plus the following 2-byte length field.
Because the guard in step 10 did not fire, this second discard advances `pos` by 32 while only 30 actual bytes remain. The parser state is now two bytes past the end of the 120-byte heap buffer.
Sink step. `PEEK_UINT16` now reads two bytes from the invalid `pos` produced by step 11, matching the saved `READ of size 2` two bytes past the 120-byte heap allocation.

format.name: raw-cdp-frame
format.contract: The witnessed 120-byte frame must reach `cdp_decode()` with Ethernet length field `0x006a`, LLC protocol `0x2000`, version byte `0x01`, and an Addresses TLV whose header bytes are `00 02 00 4d`. That TLV must begin with address count `0x20202020`, encode a first address subframe whose 16-bit address length field is `0x0020`, and leave a second subframe beginning with bytes `0x20 0x20` so the buggy parser derives `address_len == 32` again on iteration 2.
